title: "Copilot in Outlook and Teams"

## Introduction

Most of a working day happens in Outlook and Teams, and this is where Copilot saves the most minutes: it summarizes long e-mail threads, drafts replies, comments on the tone of a draft, and recaps meetings. In this tutorial we do each of these once.

## Summarizing an E-mail Thread

Open a thread with several replies. A *Summary by Copilot* control sits at the top of the thread; selecting it produces a summary with numbered citations that link back to the individual messages.

The citations are the useful part. For a decision or a date, click through to the message rather than trusting the summary. Follow-up questions go in the Copilot pane:

```         
What was asked of me in this thread, and by when?
```

## Drafting a Reply

When replying, you will see a small chat icon appear on the left hand side which allows you to *Draft with Copilot*. Here you can describe the reply rather than writing it:

```         
Reply confirming that we will send the updated fiscal tables by Friday, ask whether they also need the debt projections, and keep it to four sentences. Professional tone.
```

The draft comes with controls for tone and length, and *Regenerate* for another version. Please make sure you read it once before sending: Copilot sometimes commits you to things that were not in the prompt.

## Coaching by Copilot

For an e-mail you have written yourself, Copilot can comment instead of rewriting. Write a draft, select the Copilot icon and choose *Coaching by Copilot*. It returns suggestions on tone, clarity and how the reader is likely to receive it.

This is the better tool for anything sensitive. The words stay yours; Copilot only tells you how they land.

## Recapping a Teams Meeting

Copilot in a Teams meeting needs the meeting to be transcribed, unless the organizer has enabled Copilot without transcription. During the meeting, *Open Copilot* in the meeting controls gives a running recap:

```         
Recap the meeting so far.
```

```         
What questions have been raised and not yet answered?
```

After the meeting, the *Recap* tab of the meeting has a Copilot button for the same questions:

```         
List the action items with an owner and a deadline for each. If no deadline was given, say so.
```

Attribution is where recaps go wrong: an action item ends up with the person who mentioned it rather than the person who agreed to do it. Confirm owners in the meeting chat.

## Catching Up on Chats and Channels

In a Teams chat or channel, the Copilot button at the top right opens a pane that summarizes what you missed:

```         
Summarize the last seven days of this chat and list anything addressed to me.
```

## What to Watch For

-   **Summaries drop nuance.** A thread in which someone politely disagreed can come out as "the team agreed". Use the citations.
-   **Drafts over-commit.** Check that the reply promises only what you told it to.
-   **Meetings.** Participants can see when a meeting is transcribed; follow the Fund's rules on recording and on what Copilot may be used for in meetings with outside parties.

You've now used Copilot on the four things that fill a working day: threads, replies, tone and meetings. The next tutorial covers the standalone Copilot Chat app, which can search across all of these at once.
